The trial establishes the software change as the reason for fewer errors.
The reduction in errors probably reflects factors unrelated to the software change.
The trial provides little reason to connect the change with the error reduction.
items.answer: The software change may have contributed to the reduction in booking errors.

rationales.The software change may have contributed: 'May have contributed' reports a possible influence while leaving room for the other factors.

items.setupText: You ask a colleague at the same level to review a long draft as a favor. You want to make clear that they can decline if busy.

findings: The schedule/policy-review item repeated the long request and falsely claimed grammatical uniqueness.

items.setupText: You have reported a faulty office lock twice. A third email must be firm, request repair by Friday, and avoid accusations about anyone's motives.

audit.pedagogicalValue: Combines reference to prior contact, an unresolved problem, and a firm deadline.

audit.similarityNote: An escalated third contact, distinct from an initial repair request or a routine reminder.

items.setupText: Residents say a contractor damaged a wall. An inspection has not yet established the cause. A local newsletter needs a neutral report.

The contractor's damage to the wall was reported by several residents.
Residents have discovered how the contractor damaged the wall during the work.
The contractor apparently damaged the wall, as concerned residents have now confirmed.
items.answer: Residents say the contractor damaged the wall; the cause has not been confirmed.

rationales.Residents have discovered how the contra: 'Discovered how' implies the contractor's responsibility and the mechanism are already known.
rationales.Residents say the contractor damaged the: This attributes the account to residents and explicitly preserves the unresolved status of the cause.

findings: The notice/manager-briefing item repeated a basic formal request and attached generic criticism to every wrong option.
audit.pedagogicalValue: Separates what people report from what the publication can state as established.
audit.levelReason: A two-clause news sentence requires B2 control of source and certainty.
audit.similarityNote: Reports a disputed account for a public audience rather than drawing a research conclusion.

items.setupText: Your company entered a customer's address incorrectly. A draft apology says, 'An error occurred in the address.' The company wants to acknowledge its own action clearly.

audit.microSkill: Explicit agency in an institutional apology

items.setupText: A help page says, 'Local changes will not propagate until connectivity is restored.' Here, this means offline edits reach other devices only after the internet reconnects.

audit.pedagogicalValue: Preserves a speaker's uncertainty when converting a spoken comment into a written update.
audit.levelReason: Register shift plus modality and causal meaning creates a B2 editing demand.
audit.similarityNote: A get-passive paraphrase; it does not label the conversational form ungrammatical.

rationales.Mara expressed reservations about Sunday: This replaces conversational wording with neutral reporting while keeping both parts of her position.

items.setupText: Engineers estimate a website will be available again at 3 p.m., but the time is not confirmed. You write a customer update.

audit.levelReason: Calibrating a service message's commitment while preserving information suits B2.

items.setupText: A report draft says, 'The pilot reduced costs. That said, it required extra staff time.' The editor wants a more formal linking expression.

The pilot reduced costs. In other words, it required extra staff time.

rationales.The pilot reduced costs. However, it req: 'However' provides a formal contrast, preserving the shift from a benefit to a limitation.

items.setupText: An organization has established that its late cancellation cost participants money. It wants a formal apology acknowledging that specific harm, without making a compensation promise.
items.taskText: Which apology best meets that brief?

We apologize for the financial loss our late cancellation caused participants.
We regret that participants believe the cancellation caused them financial loss.
We apologize for the cancellation and will reimburse the losses participants incurred.
items.answer: We apologize for the financial loss our late cancellation caused participants.
items.explanation: This acknowledges the organization's action and its established consequence directly without promising reimbursement.

rationales.We apologize if our cancellation caused: 'If' treats harm as uncertain, and 'inconvenience' avoids the established financial consequence.
rationales.We regret that participants believe the: This makes participants' belief the object of regret and distances the organization from the established harm.
rationales.We apologize for the financial loss our: This acknowledges the organization's action and its established consequence directly without promising reimbursement.
rationales.We apologize for the cancellation and wi: This adds a compensation commitment that the brief does not authorize.

findings: The report/committee-review item reduced C1 to choosing a stock apology over casual wording; wrong feedback was identical.
audit.microSkill: Apology acknowledging established harm without an added commitment
audit.pedagogicalValue: Distinguishes direct responsibility from conditional or belief-focused apology language.
audit.levelReason: Tracks factual status, interpersonal stance, and commitment within closely related formal options.

items.setupText: An internal review found no evidence that files were copied, but incomplete logs prevent ruling copying out. You draft a careful incident summary.
items.taskText: Which sentence keeps the distinction between missing evidence and proof of non-occurrence?
options: We confirmed that no files were copied, although some logs were incomplete.
The incomplete logs indicate that files were probably copied during the incident.
We found no evidence of copying and can therefore rule out that possibility.
We found no evidence of copying, although the incomplete logs limit that conclusion.
items.answer: We found no evidence of copying, although the incomplete logs limit that conclusion.
items.explanation: This reports the review's finding and its evidential limit without claiming copying did not occur.

rationales.We found no evidence of copying, althoug: This reports the review's finding and its evidential limit without claiming copying did not occur.
rationales.We confirmed that no files were copied,: 'Confirmed that no files were copied' makes a stronger claim than the incomplete record supports.

rationales.We found no evidence of copying and can: This treats absence of evidence as sufficient proof of absence despite the stated limitation.

findings: The schedule/methodology-section item had an incoherent tail and a false single-correct-sentence setup; its decision was below C1.
audit.pedagogicalValue: Maintains a limitation when reporting a negative finding in an authoritative voice.
audit.levelReason: The required distinction concerns inference and evidential scope, suitable for C1.
audit.similarityNote: A negative finding from incomplete records, unlike a tentative positive causal finding.

items.setupText: A reviewer correctly notes that your study cannot establish causation. You still think its association finding is useful and must respond constructively.
items.taskText: Choose a response that accepts the limitation while preserving the narrower contribution.
options: We appreciate the comment, but the strength of the association establishes the causal claim.
We agree that causation is not established; the association nevertheless merits further investigation.
We accept the limitation and have removed the association finding from our discussion.
We regret that the reviewer has interpreted our causal evidence as a mere association.
items.answer: We agree that causation is not established; the association nevertheless merits further investigation.
items.explanation: This concedes the valid limitation while identifying a defensible role for the remaining finding.

rationales.We appreciate the comment, but the stren: The polite opening does not fix the unsupported move from association to causation.
rationales.We accept the limitation and have remove: This gives up the narrower finding instead of explaining its continuing value.
rationales.We regret that the reviewer has interpre: This challenges the reviewer on a point the scenario says is correct and upgrades the evidence to causal.
rationales.We agree that causation is not establish: This concedes the valid limitation while identifying a defensible role for the remaining finding.

findings: The form/stakeholder-meeting apology repeated a simple formula and framed a register judgment as grammaticality.
audit.microSkill: Constructive concession in a reviewer response
audit.pedagogicalValue: Acknowledges a valid criticism without either overstating the evidence or abandoning a narrower contribution.
audit.levelReason: Balancing concession, stance, and a bounded contribution suits C1 academic correspondence.
audit.similarityNote: A response to criticism with an explicitly valid point, not an initial research claim.

items.setupText: Asked specifically about a candidate's strategic leadership, a referee writes only, 'She is unfailingly punctual and keeps meticulous attendance records.'

options: It directly establishes that she lacks the strategic leadership skills required for the role.
It strongly endorses her leadership through specific examples of strategic decision-making.
It praises reliability while leaving the requested leadership assessment unanswered.
It criticizes her reliability by using language that is clearly sarcastic in this context.
items.answer: It praises reliability while leaving the requested leadership assessment unanswered.
items.explanation: The positive details concern reliability; their failure to address leadership may be telling, but no explicit leadership judgment is made.

rationales.It praises reliability while leaving the: The positive details concern reliability; their failure to address leadership may be telling, but no explicit leadership judgment is made.
rationales.It strongly endorses her leadership thro: Punctuality and attendance records are not examples of strategic decision-making.
rationales.It criticizes her reliability by using l: The context supports a limited endorsement, but it does not establish sarcasm about reliability.

findings: The notice/recommendation-issued item repeated a stock apology and offered no advanced interpretation of implied meaning.
audit.pedagogicalValue: Distinguishes a possible implication from an explicitly stated negative judgment.
audit.levelReason: Reading what a formal reference leaves unsaid without over-inference is suitable C1 practice.
audit.similarityNote: Interprets restricted praise in a reference rather than explicit disagreement or refusal.

items.setupText: Researchers write, 'The estimate is imprecise and should not be interpreted as evidence of no effect.' For this task, that means the result cannot settle whether an effect exists.
items.taskText: Choose the plain-language public summary that preserves that uncertainty.
options: The result shows no effect, although its exact size remains uncertain.
The result points to an effect that a larger study will probably confirm.
The result is uncertain because the researchers chose an unsuitable method.
The result is too uncertain to tell us whether there is an effect.
items.answer: The result is too uncertain to tell us whether there is an effect.
items.explanation: This translates the limitation into everyday language without treating uncertainty as either proof or disproof.

rationales.The result is too uncertain to tell us w: This translates the limitation into everyday language without treating uncertainty as either proof or disproof.

findings: The email/evidence-compared version used academic context words around a basic apology and repeated feedback.

audit.pedagogicalValue: Preserves uncertainty when removing specialist phrasing for a public audience.

items.setupText: After several interruptions, a meeting chair says, 'Could we allow Leila to finish her explanation before returning to questions?'
items.taskText: Which interpretation best captures the chair's immediate communicative purpose?
options: The chair is asking Leila whether she is capable of finishing her explanation.
The chair is inviting a vote on whether Leila's explanation deserves to continue.
The chair is directing the group to postpone questions until Leila has finished.
The chair is suggesting that Leila finish privately after the meeting has ended.
items.answer: The chair is directing the group to postpone questions until Leila has finished.

rationales.The chair is inviting a vote on whether: The wording manages the speaking order; it does not propose a vote on Leila's contribution.
rationales.The chair is directing the group to post: The interrogative 'Could we' softens a chair's direction about turn-taking; 'before' specifies the order.

audit.pedagogicalValue: Interprets an inclusive modal question in light of a chair's role and the preceding interruptions.
audit.levelReason: Combining authority, discourse history, and indirect wording creates a C1 pragmatic demand.
audit.similarityNote: An institutional intervention restoring a speaker's turn, beyond a personal polite interruption.

items.setupText: A draft says, 'With respect, your calculation ignores the delivery charge.' You want to challenge the omission while reducing the personal edge.

rationales.With all due respect, you appear to have: 'Fairly obvious' sharpens the personal criticism; the courtesy phrase does not cancel it.
rationales.Your calculation is quite interesting, a: This softens the message until the known omission becomes an optional general consideration.

rationales.The calculation omits the delivery charg: This identifies the specific omission and requests a correction without evaluating the person's competence.

findings: The application/evaluation-form item repeated a simple apology and attached a grammar instruction to a register task.
audit.microSkill: Reducing the personal edge of formal disagreement
audit.pedagogicalValue: Shows that courtesy markers do not neutralize evaluative criticism of the recipient.
audit.levelReason: Evaluating the effect of disclaimers and targeted wording suits C1 interpersonal editing.
audit.similarityNote: Revises a seemingly polite preface that can intensify rather than reduce disagreement.

items.setupText: A handbook says, 'Employees may request a review of the decision.' In this handbook, 'may' grants permission; it does not predict what employees will do.

items.setupText: A company mistakenly deleted customer records. A draft says, 'A data housekeeping exercise resulted in some records becoming unavailable.' The company wants a candid statement of what it did.

items.answer: We mistakenly deleted customer records during a data-cleaning operation.

audit.pedagogicalValue: Identifies how abstract descriptions can conceal an action and replace a fact with the audience's reaction.

audit.similarityNote: Unpacks several layers of an obscuring draft rather than merely replacing a passive verb.

items.setupText: You summarize an author's argument without signaling either approval or skepticism. The draft says, 'The author purports to explain the decline in participation.'

audit.pedagogicalValue: Distinguishes an author's aim from the editor's evaluation of its success or sincerity.

items.setupText: A consumer leaflet must explain a supplied policy: customers are entitled to a refund if an item arrives damaged. A conversational draft says, 'We'll sort you out if it turns up broken.'

rationales.Customers should contact us if they beli: This gives a contact instruction but does not state the refund entitlement.

audit.levelReason: Distinguishing a right from an offer or contact instruction requires C1 precision.

items.setupText: A report arrived after the deadline. Its accuracy has not yet been checked. You need to criticize the lateness without implying anything about accuracy.

The report should be treated as provisional because it missed the submission deadline.
items.answer: The report was submitted late; its accuracy remains to be assessed.
items.explanation: This records the process failure and separates it from the still-open question about content.

rationales.The report's lateness raises doubts abou: This links late delivery to questionable accuracy, which has not been assessed.
rationales.The report was submitted late; its accur: This records the process failure and separates it from the still-open question about content.
rationales.Although submitted late, the report prov: This uses concession to endorse accuracy before it has been checked.
rationales.The report should be treated as provisio: This makes the content's status depend on lateness rather than the uncompleted accuracy review.

findings: The survey/risk-assessment tail was unnatural and the item repeated a stock apology with generic rationales.

audit.pedagogicalValue: Prevents one justified criticism from implying a second unsupported judgment.

items.setupText: You invite an external expert to a panel. They have not agreed. You want a courteous closing that leaves participation optional.

items.answer: We would be delighted if you were able to join the panel.

rationales.Thank you for agreeing to share your exp: This explicitly states agreement that has not been given.
rationales.We would be delighted if you were able t: The conditional wording expresses enthusiasm while making participation depend on the expert's ability and choice.

items.answer: The suspension nevertheless delayed applications, irrespective of the inquiry's subsequent finding.

findings: The proposal/final-vote item repeated a formulaic apology and a false claim of single-sentence correctness.
audit.microSkill: Precise retrospective reference and causal chronology
audit.pedagogicalValue: Uses explicit event reference to prevent confusion between a prior decision and a later finding.

items.setupText: A colleague tells you privately that a close friend has died. You want to express sympathy without claiming to know their feelings or asking them to explain.

items.answer: I'm sorry to hear that. There's no need to reply to this message.

audit.pedagogicalValue: Calibrates warmth and restraint in a sensitive personal exchange.

items.setupText: Your mixed British and American team uses 'table a proposal' differently: some mean introduce it for discussion, others mean set it aside. You intend to delay discussion until June.
items.taskText: Choose wording that states that intention unambiguously for this team.

items.setupText: A restaurant review says, 'The soup arrived after forty-five minutes. Service, it seems, is an exercise in patience.' The reviewer intends a restrained criticism of the wait.

The reviewer criticized the slow service, citing a forty-five-minute wait for soup.

The passage transcribes the guest's public complaint to the ceremony's organizers.
The formal narrator objectively endorses the ceremony's emphasis on public speaking.
The incomplete sentences indicate accidental editing errors that prevent the attitude from being understood.
items.answer: The short, ironic units bring the narration close to the guest's unspoken irritation.
items.explanation: The fragments and mock approval echo the character's private reactions, giving the narrative an immediate, conversational quality without making them spoken dialogue.
